default.reason: No terminal-edition implementation evidence is mapped for this desktop capability yet.

Material Design 3 (M3 Expressive) shell.reason: The Textual shell carries the hierarchy, tonal surfaces, focus states, density, theme, and responsive intent that a terminal can render; pixel, font, elevation, ripple, and compositor effects remain terminal-owned.

Navigation rail.reason: A mouse-clickable repository rail and keyboard-reachable workspace tabs replace the graphical icon rail.

Floating pill toolbar.reason: The active repository, branch divergence, fetch, pull, push, and editor actions are exposed in a terminal toolbar.

Measured toolbar overflow.reason: The layout has compact and narrow breakpoints, but does not yet provide the desktop edition's measured More-menu migration contract.

Light / dark / system theme.reason: Light and dark themes apply live and the system choice persists; automatic terminal/system theme detection is not yet complete.

Per-element appearance editors.reason: Settings provides live, persisted foreground, background, emphasis, and border overrides for six terminal surfaces, plus reset and settings history. Contextual per-owner invocation, repository/tab-specific owners, and font, size, radius, and spacing controls are absent.

Git-backed appearance history.reason: Whole-config snapshots use one isolated XDG Git repository with in-app browse, read, restore, undo, and redo. Separate repositories and setting.json histories per appearance owner are absent.

UI font customization.reason: The terminal emulator owns font family, point size, glyph fallback, and weight availability; the TUI does not pretend it can override them.

Density control.reason: Comfortable and compact density are persisted and applied to terminal layout classes.

UI scale slider 50–200% + auto-fit.reason: Cell size and zoom belong to the terminal emulator. The app reflows at narrow widths instead of claiming control over terminal zoom.

Material re-tint of stock surfaces.reason: Textual widgets use the TUI token stylesheet for dark/light, accent, focus, error, and surface roles.

Universal button hint.reason: Primary shell buttons expose labels and selected tooltips, but complete tooltip coverage is not yet mapped.

Exhaustive responsive gate.reason: Narrow and compact layout breakpoints exist. The dated Linux PTY and mouse run remains the acceptance authority and must not be inferred from source.

Three language modes.reason: English, playful Hong Kong Cantonese, and compact bilingual modes persist with English fallback, and the shell plus shared controls localize. Most repository, GitHub, Advanced, and notification copy remains English-only.

Funny-level sliders (1–5).reason: Independent persisted English and Cantonese choices from 1 to 5 are exposed, and every catalog entry that offers tone variants now produces distinct output at all five positions without changing facts. A substantial amount of repository and provider copy remains outside the shared tone catalog, so the whole product is not yet wired.

Spoken narrator.reason: The off-by-default preference, language, quiet hours, reduced sound, and screen-reader-yield controls persist; speech execution and serialized playback are not yet implemented.

Quiet hours, reduced sound, and screen-r.reason: The preferences persist and the startup dim-sum card obeys the configured quiet-hours window. Narrator playback policy is not yet active.

The dim sum surprise.reason: An exactly-once fresh 10% launch draw selects from the verified bundled catalog, renders the local PNG as bounded terminal true-color blocks with bilingual factual names and alt text, never steals focus, auto-dismisses, and suppresses first-run, error, update, modal, and quiet-hours launches without a later ambush or opt-out.

Repository tabs.reason: Repository tabs now restore from a profile-keyed SQLite SessionRecord, keep a stable manual order, expose aliases and metadata, and remain mouse- and keyboard-selectable through a bounded terminal strip plus the complete Tabs pane.

Tab groups.reason: Named groups, membership editing, contiguous group blocks, pin-boundary validation, and persisted collapse/expand state are live. Curated group colors and the desktop chip/member-popover presentation are not reproduced in the terminal edition.

Group persistence boundaries.reason: Group membership survives restart and tab close, collapsed groups persist in the profile-keyed SessionRecord, imports preserve existing destination groups, and named groups cannot cross the pin boundary. Repository group membership remains shared by the local repository record rather than duplicated per window.

Pin, favourite, and manual arrange.reason: The terminal Tabs pane persists pin and favourite state, moves tabs or named groups through keyboard-reachable up/down actions, and offers one-shot label, opened-time, repository-status, and favourites sorts without continuously reshuffling later.

Search tabs / Arrange tabs.reason: A dedicated Tabs pane searches visible labels, aliases, groups, names, and paths with the shared literal, fuzzy, and bounded RE2 control, while manual movement and persisted one-shot arrangements keep named groups together.

Close Tabs Containing… and its guarded i.reason: Both close predicates use one synchronized literal/fuzzy/RE2 search state, show bounded live close/keep/protected counts, reject empty, invalid, or zero-match reviews, exclude pinned tabs by default, require an explicit review checkbox, and recheck working-tree and commit-draft safety immediately before closing only the session tabs.

Tab-strip overflow dropdown.reason: The terminal strip keeps pinned and active entries visible within a bounded capacity, reports the overflow count on a persistent Tabs button, and opens the complete searchable tab list where every overflowed or collapsed repository remains activatable and manageable.

Tab session export / import.reason: The Tabs pane atomically exports and imports bounded UTF-8 JSON with stable order, active repository, aliases, pins, and favourites; imports merge or replace open tabs while preserving existing destination groups. Per-tab graphical appearance is not part of the terminal session format.

Clone, add local, create repository.reason: Open and Create combine real path inputs with a folder-only mouse/keyboard browser; Clone uses a real normalized destination input. All three use argv-safe Git calls, and matching outer quotes are removed from pasted paths without shell evaluation.

Repository list filter and alias.reason: The repository rail and complete Tabs pane render persisted per-repository aliases and filter aliases, names, paths, and group names through the shared literal, fuzzy, and bounded RE2 search service.

Worktree management.reason: The Advanced pane lists, adds, locks and unlocks with optional reasons, moves, renames, repairs, removes, and prunes worktrees. Branch, start-point, detached, and force controls plus typed removal confirmation are wired to bounded argv-only Git operations.

Submodule add and management.reason: The Advanced pane lists, initializes or updates, synchronizes, and guardedly deinitializes existing submodules with repository-relative path validation. Provider/account-aware add, streamed progress, and cancellation are not implemented.

Guided sparse checkout.reason: The Advanced pane reads, applies, and disables cone or non-cone sparse patterns through editable controls and typed confirmation. The desktop three-step review flow and state-specific guide are not reproduced.

Remote management.reason: The repository service supports safe remote list/add/remove operations, while the terminal surface does not yet reproduce every desktop remote-management workflow.

Repository Tools panel.reason: Searchable remote and tag inventory plus worktree, submodule, sparse-checkout, reflog, and repository-diagnostics surfaces are reachable. Patch-series, planned commit rewriting, signing, Git LFS administration, and guided bisect are absent.

Release-backed Cheap LFS.reason: The terminal edition reads and writes canonical v1 Release pointers and provides preview, explicit confirmed Track uploads, and cache-first restore. Its Git wrapper adds source-history preflight and post-pull materialization but never stages, commits, uploads, or rewrites automatically. Automatic open/clone integration, cancelable confirmed transfers, bucket rollover, browser handoff, and the desktop account-bound background workflows are absent.

Cheap LFS asset versioning.reason: Content-derived immutable asset names, exact provider proofs, provenance labels, and ordinary Git pointer history preserve versions without clobbering an existing asset. Post-commit asset relabeling, cross-name content reuse, an in-app version browser, and the desktop lifecycle tooling are absent.

Large files manager.reason: A mouse- and keyboard-reachable Cheap LFS tab provides searchable inventory, real path/tag/repository text fields, a plan TextArea, and clickable Preview, Track, Verify, and Restore actions with typed mutation confirmation. Batch materialization, removal, the desktop settings set, and the complete state/filter surface are absent.

Oversized-file filter and two-lane clone.reason: Cheap LFS inventory identifies safe files strictly over 100 MiB; the Git wrapper blocks working-tree bypass candidates and oversized source-history blobs, verifies indexed materialized payloads, and restores pointers after explicit pulls. The Changes filter, automatic clone/open repair, and desktop two-lane 90% look-ahead coordinator are absent.

Permanent discard.reason: Selected-file discard is confirmation gated and names the target; the complete desktop permanent-discard surface is not yet present.

Stage by file, hunk, or line; commit; am.reason: File staging, unstaging, commit summary/body text boxes, sign-off, amend, and commit-and-push exist. Hunk/line staging and undo are not yet implemented.

Co-authors, revert, cherry-pick, squash,.reason: The commit composer validates and writes multiple Co-authored-by trailers, and selected History commits have reviewed revert and cherry-pick actions. Squash and reorder are not yet implemented.

Effective Git author disclosure.reason: The commit composer resolves the effective user.name and user.email through Git, then discloses each value's active scope and origin before a commit is created. Missing values remain explicit instead of being replaced with placeholders.

Copilot commit-message controls.reason: The composer provides deterministic concise or detailed offline drafts from bounded staged metadata and preserves a non-empty user draft behind confirmation. No Copilot provider, model selector, provider telemetry, or network claim exists, so this is deliberately presented as offline assistance rather than Copilot.

History search and dedicated lane graph.reason: History searches bounded commit messages, authors, hashes, and decorations across the current branch or all refs, and identifies merge rows. A graphical lane graph is not reproduced in the terminal yet.

Advanced history discovery.reason: The History pane switches between current-branch and read-only all-ref discovery, loads bounded 100-record pages, searches ref decorations, and exposes exact selected-commit checkout, branch, and tag actions. All-ref mode disables branch-mutating revert and cherry-pick actions.

Selection-aware commit context menu.reason: A selected History row drives keyboard-reachable copy, reviewed revert/cherry-pick, detached checkout, create-branch, and create-tag actions. The terminal surface does not yet provide a context menu or selection-aware squash, reorder, and reset actions.

Merge commits in History.reason: History parses parent cardinality, keeps merge commits in both current and all-ref result sets, and marks them with a distinct merge kind and terminal emphasis without changing their factual message.

File history.reason: History accepts a repository-bound file path, follows renames through bounded Git log output, and offers a bounded blame view with author and line detail.

Stashing.reason: Named stash creation, apply, pop, and guarded drop are exposed through buttons and text input.

Selective stashes.reason: The stash pane accepts an exact newline-delimited set of whole files, shows that set for review before Git runs, and the service rejects paths outside the repository before constructing literal pathspec arguments.

Named multi-stash manager.reason: The pane creates, inspects, applies, pops, branches from, and guardedly drops multiple named stashes. Every selected action revalidates the exact object ID before Git runs; stash rename and explicit retained partial-failure receipts are not yet implemented.

External stash interoperability.reason: The pane reads externally created Git stashes, inspects their exact object and patch, and can apply, pop, branch from, or explicitly guardedly drop them. Every action revalidates ref-to-object identity and does not rewrite stash metadata.

Branch create, rename, delete, switch, a.reason: The branches pane exposes create, rename, switch, guarded delete, and stale-checked reviewed merge. Merge-tree reports conflicting paths before mutation, and any confirmed Git conflicts remain visible in Changes for explicit resolution.

Reviewed bulk branch deletion.reason: A bounded multi-selection review excludes current, default, protected, and checked-out worktree branches, displays every exact branch tip, and revalidates all refs before deleting any. Each successful deletion reports its retained recovery object ID, while stale or failed candidates remain isolated and visible.

Branch pin, hide, solo, and restore.reason: The Branches pane provides pin/unpin, hide, solo, restore-hidden, and default-branch actions backed by atomic repository-scoped XDG persistence outside the repository. Named preference presets and import/export are not yet present.

Branch sorting.reason: The Branches pane switches live between last-activity and alphabetical ordering. The choice is not yet persisted or exposed from Settings → Appearance.

Publish indicator for local-only branche.reason: Each branch row and detail view distinguish published, local-only, remote, and configured-upstream-gone states from real for-each-ref metadata.

Merge-tree conflict preview.reason: A clean-tree preview computes current, source, merge-base, incoming commits, changed files, and exact merge-tree conflict paths without changing index or worktree. Confirmation revalidates both reviewed tips before merging.

Reviewed ordinary pull previews.reason: The Branches pane fetches the configured upstream, displays the exact local and fetched object IDs, integration route, bounded incoming commits, and changed files, then revalidates route and refs before the confirmed pull runs. Dirty trees and ambiguous upstreams are refused before mutation.

Deleted-upstream pull recovery.reason: An explicit recovery action proves the configured upstream is absent with ls-remote, reviews switching to the default branch, and keeps deletion of the stale local branch as a separate opt-in. Failed pulls are not yet intercepted automatically and there is no batch recovery surface.

Reviewed rebase onto a searched target.reason: A terminal target field accepts an exact local branch, remote ref, or tag, previews current/target object IDs and bounded replay commits, refuses dirty trees, and revalidates both tips immediately before the confirmed rebase. It never pushes or rewrites an unreviewed target.

Reviewed batch repository sync.reason: The Sync & integrate tab validates an exact newline-delimited repository subset, reviews fetch or pull per repository, caps concurrency at three, supports cancellation between commands, and reports isolated per-repository results without shell execution.

Pull all repositories.reason: Reviewed batch sync can pull every explicitly listed validated repository with bounded concurrency, cancellation, and isolated outcomes. It does not yet discover every persisted repository automatically or retry ambiguous multi-account credentials.

Deepen or unshallow.reason: History detects shallow state and provides reviewed bounded deepen and unshallow operations against the current repository. Credential-helper failures remain visible, but the desktop edition's signed-in account re-authentication route is absent.

Tag creation.reason: Repository Tools provides keyboard- and mouse-operable tag name, target commit, and optional annotation inputs backed by validated local Git tag creation, plus typed-confirm local deletion.

Complete tag lifecycle.reason: Local inventory, lightweight or annotated creation on an exact commit, and typed-confirm deletion are exposed and tested. Move, sign, push, fetch, prune, remote deletion, and recovery receipts are not yet implemented.

Merge all branches or worktrees.reason: A bounded review enumerates exact local-branch and registered-worktree tips, refuses dirty worktrees and predicted merge-tree conflicts, and revalidates every source before sequential merges with per-target receipts. Automated conflict resolution and editable AI output are not present.

Git operation auto-fix.reason: Repository failures are classified from bounded text and produce a visible recovery prompt containing the exact operation and error while forbidding force-push, history rewrite, commit dropping, branch switching, ref deletion, reset, discard, and implicit stashing. No automatic remediation action runs yet.

Text diffs with syntax highlighting and.reason: The Changes pane exposes ordinary or native Git word diffs, plain copyable patches or Rich diff-syntax highlighting, and bounded context selection. Every mode reads the same exact repository path and staged/working-tree side.

Image diffs.reason: Exact before/after bytes for supported PNG changes render locally as bounded true-color terminal half blocks. The dependency-free decoder rejects oversized, corrupt, interlaced, palette, grayscale, TGA, SVG, and other unsupported image inputs without executing or fetching content.

Changed-file tree view.reason: Changes switches live between the multi-select flat list and a deterministic directory tree. Only bounded, control-free repository-relative paths are grouped; unsafe labels remain inert root leaves, and file actions retain the exact original Git path.

Expanded diff context.reason: A live diff control selects 3, 20, 50, 100, or a bounded 10,000 context lines and reloads the exact staged or working-tree patch without modifying repository state.

Structured CSV and TSV diffs.reason: Bounded UTF-8 CSV and TSV previews parse quoting, CRLF/LF, embedded newlines, row insertion/removal, and changed cells into a semantic terminal table. The table is presentation-only, and malformed, binary, or over-limit input fails closed without generating a patch.

Sandboxed Markdown previews.reason: Bounded repository-confined UTF-8 Markdown renders through Textual's terminal-native parser, which has no browser DOM or script execution. Automatic link opening is disabled and image syntax remains inert alt text, so previewing performs no network or filesystem navigation.

Pull-request list and branch checkout.reason: The pull-request list opens a bounded detail workspace with exact head/base refs, review state, activity counts, changed-file metadata, and patch inspection. Fork discovery and branch checkout are still not implemented.

Check runs and CI status.reason: Selecting a pull request loads its exact head SHA, then combines paginated latest check runs with legacy commit statuses under one 500-item cap. The TUI exposes source, state, conclusion, timestamps, bounded summary text, and the GitHub details URL.

In-app pull-request review workspace.reason: The terminal workspace loads bounded pull-request details, changed files and patches, checks/statuses, conversation activity, and review comments; it submits explicit approve/comment/request-changes reviews and exact-head line comments. Thread replies/resolution, code-suggestion authoring, full diff context expansion, and internal suggestion workflows remain unavailable.

In-app pull-request creation.reason: Base, head, title, and body are editable in real terminal inputs and submitted through the bounded GitHub service. Template discovery, draft and maintainer controls, provider metadata, and exact-account selection are absent.

Pull-request lifecycle.reason: Creation and reviewed merge remain available; reviews are now explicit approve/comment/request-changes mutations bound to the loaded head SHA, and line comments require an exact file, side, and diff line. Thread replies/resolution, account selection, branch checkout, and the desktop edition's broader lifecycle controls remain unavailable.

Pull-request activity notifications.reason: A repository-scoped GitHub notification inbox lists, searches, and inspects up to 500 threads and can mark only the selected numeric thread as read. Operating-system delivery, failed-check routing, and cross-source de-duplication are not implemented.

Branch and repository rules.reason: The TUI can inspect, search, and render the parameters of up to 500 active repository- and organization-level rules that effectively apply to one exact branch. Raw ruleset inventory, disabled/evaluate rules, wildcard-target inspection, and ruleset mutation are not implemented.

GitHub Projects workspace.reason: A read-only project inventory is available when the token has project scope; mutation and offline workspace parity are not implemented.

GitHub Issues.reason: Issue list, detail, creation, comments, state changes, and close operations are exposed; advanced triage parity remains incomplete.

Actions run browser.reason: Workflow and run tables provide keyboard/mouse selection, refresh, bounded text/regex search, visible event data, and dedicated workflow, branch, event, and status filters backed by the GitHub Actions REST query.

Job, step, and log inspection.reason: Selecting a run loads its jobs and run-log metadata; selecting a job renders every reported step, and job log text is fetched through a strict byte and timeout bound into a scrollable inspector.

Re-run all or failed jobs.reason: The selected run exposes separate full-rerun and failed-jobs-only controls, both mapped to the matching GitHub Actions REST endpoints and covered by fake-transport and UI tests.

Workflow dispatch with inputs.reason: Workflow dispatch accepts a ref plus a validated JSON object of up to 25 scalar input values. Workflow-file input-schema discovery and generated choice/boolean controls are not yet present.

Cancel workflow runs.reason: Selected run cancellation is confirmation gated. Cancellable-status and identity revalidation, duplicate suppression, a complete target summary, and polling until terminal state are absent.

Actions caches.reason: The cache tab paginates real Actions cache metadata, provides bounded text/regex search, and requires review plus typed cache-id confirmation before ID-scoped deletion. Cache archive download is explicitly unavailable because GitHub exposes no supported archive-download endpoint.

Actions artifacts.reason: The artifact tab paginates repository or run artifacts, provides bounded text/regex search, rejects expired or oversized archives, and saves only SHA-256-verified bytes to a non-existing destination through the no-shell gh transport.

Repository Releases dashboard.reason: Release inventory, detail, draft creation, editing, publish, typed-confirmation deletion, asset inventory, and bounded asset download with SHA-256 verification when GitHub supplies a digest are available. Multipart asset upload and the desktop dashboard's complete filtering remain unavailable and are labeled in the pane.

GitHub Packages explorer.reason: Package inventory and selected-package version metadata are exposed with local search. GitHub's Packages REST API does not provide registry content download, so file transfer remains explicitly delegated to each package type's registry-native client.

GitHub API rail.reason: The terminal GitHub pane includes bounded REST and GraphQL request inputs plus a scrollable response viewer. Automatic action catalogs and hide/reveal behavior are absent.

Fuzzy / substring / regex filter modes.reason: The shared search bar provides literal, fuzzy, and explicit RE2 modes with synchronized flags across repository, GitHub, notification, Settings, and changelog collections.

Safe RE2 regex builder.reason: The builder composes literals, classes, anchors, groups, alternation, and quantifiers; exposes raw editing and flags; and evaluates bounded sample text with google-re2.

Regex builder reflow.reason: The match/sample split participates in the terminal's generic narrow layout. Compact-height scrolling and explicit preservation of the token grid, tester, and footer are not implemented or accepted.

Command palette.reason: Ctrl+P opens a literal, fuzzy, or regex-searchable palette with 50 real commands and exact Settings destinations in five groups, keyboard focus, clickable rows, and a persisted bounded/full-window size. The desktop palette's 87 fully localized commands and richer inline setting controls remain absent.

Command-palette appearance editor.reason: The palette persists a user-selected bounded-card or full-terminal presentation and applies it live. Per-element typography, colour, spacing, and shape editing from the desktop appearance editor are not implemented.

Settings search.reason: The mounted Settings tab searches English and Cantonese names, descriptions, keywords, and current values through literal, fuzzy, or bounded RE2 modes; every result focuses its exact control and the full builder returns to the originating field.

Dialog wheel and trackpad scrolling.reason: Scrollable Textual containers handle terminal wheel events and keyboard scrolling, but nested edge chaining and real trackpad acceptance are not implemented or evidenced.

Non-blocking error notices.reason: Informational and non-decision errors use corner notifications while confirmations remain decision dialogs. The user-selectable traditional blocking-error mode is absent.

Notification centre.reason: A searchable, reviewable SQLite-backed history supports read state and clear-all confirmation. Event filters, visible-result selection, bulk unread/delete, bell/side-sheet presentation, and Git-backed recovery are absent.

MD3 Preferences dialog.reason: A terminal-native Settings tab exposes appearance, language, interaction, editor, narrator, accessibility, and history controls, plus bilingual/current-value search and exact-control navigation.

External editor discovery and opening.reason: Installed editors are detected and the configured editor opens the active repository through an argv-safe process launch.

Broad editor catalog.reason: Common Linux editors are detected, while the graphical edition's full cross-platform catalog is not reproduced.

Open in shell.reason: The Advanced pane launches the configured or auto-detected terminal in the active repository or a validated child directory using an argv-only process.

One-click Build & Run.reason: Persisted user-supplied build and run commands execute as bounded argv-only processes with repository-child working directories and captured output. Automatic project and runnable-profile discovery is not implemented.

Responsiveness and resource lifecycle.reason: Async workers keep Git/GitHub calls off the UI loop and owned database resources close on unmount; exhaustive load and cancellation acceptance remains pending.

Versioned settings history.reason: Atomic XDG configuration snapshots are committed to an isolated app-owned Git repository with in-app browse, restore, undo, and redo. Per-account ownership and the Ctrl+Alt+Z route are absent.

Safer destructive confirmations.reason: Discard, branch and stash deletion, worktree removal, sparse-checkout changes, workflow cancellation, and clearing history use decision dialogs. The desktop row's undo, reset, and tag-deletion confirmations are not all exposed.

Documentation hub.reason: A persistent terminal Help tab provides a keyboard/mouse/safety guide, a direct route to the searchable in-app release history, and a copyable live documentation URL. The desktop site's full article hierarchy and suggested-article navigation remain external.

In-app version history.reason: The Help tab embeds a bounded catalog of all 707 recorded releases with typed date filters, literal/fuzzy/RE2 search, unrecorded-date control, lazy per-release entries, commit-SHA copy, and non-overwriting Markdown export.

Categorized feature documentation.reason: The Linux TUI has a dedicated categorized documentation set covering behavior, configuration, failure modes, security, accessibility, and verification.

Regex guide.reason: The TUI search and regex document names the RE2 dialect, flags, limits, escaping, and builder/search synchronization.
